alternative_architecture.description: Reorganize around a thin, change-driven delivery controller. State: keep approved GDD requirements and immutable task-contract revisions in Git; keep one operational lifecycle ledger for planned/running/validating/blocked/review/done; treat the merge commit plus evidence manifest as delivery truth. Planning: human-prioritize one vertical slice and link it to stable requirement IDs; GDD diffs impact only linked work. Execution: one scoped writable coding worker on a branch, with checkpoint commits. Validation: deterministic Git checks, a real Windows Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode/build adapter, one semantic diff review, and explicit human visual/feel gates. Recovery: reconcile attempt IDs against branches, commits, Unity artifacts, and merges so retries are idempotent. Unity integration: maintain one validated canonical scene registry and enforce project-lock/import-cache policy. Keep the existing GDDRAG, clean Unity runner, bounded runtime, and evidence concepts; demote global reconciliation to occasional audits.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the sound safety components while putting the missing delivery transaction at the center. It also treats GDD evolution as scoped change impact rather than globally invalidating evidence or rebuilding the roadmap.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The underlying principles are sound—bounded workers, deterministic facts, Git integration truth, runtime evidence, and human design authority—but the implemented architecture is not yet sound as an autonomous game-development investment. It is a heavily hardened read/review and evidence framework surrounding a nonexistent gameplay delivery loop. Worse, evolving-canon synchronization already fails: the canonical scene moved, yet the GDD, task contracts, and resource records still reference the deleted path while graph validation passes.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: The repository cannot reveal undocumented Unity-host automation or human workflows outside Git. If a reliable external execution/build lane already exists, the delivery gap is smaller, but it is not integrated with this architecture.
do_not_build_yet: A general continuous supervisor or automatic dispatcher.
Parallel workers, claims, merge queues, and broad worktree scheduling.
Bidirectional GitHub Issues/Projects synchronization; choose one operational authority first.
Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority/Artifact GER until a real feature is blocked by missing approved design.
Provider fallback or additional provider/reviewer migrations.
Another global reconciliation or multi-model verification cycle for ordinary GDD edits.
Top-k-only compact task context; the current GDD is small enough to provide in full.
More conformance-schema hardening before a new gameplay delivery exercises the existing model.

evidence.observation: At the frozen commit, taskcontrol validation passes, but readiness is explicitly unavailable and authorization denies every task.
The conformance evaluator compares every record with a hash of the entire canonical GDD; any GDD edit makes otherwise unchanged evidence stale.
OpenAI/Codex rejects repository writing and approved command execution, so the implemented provider path cannot advance gameplay.
TaskExecution only publishes task_request.json and delegates one generic invocation; it has no planning, Git, Unity, GER, evidence-publication, or completion behavior.

The authoritative scene is now Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity, but numerous task contracts and resource locks still reference the deleted Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity.
NSC-037 still says the current authoritative scene is the deleted path and incorrectly classifies the actual authoritative scene as a non-canonical stub.
The current GDD itself still declares the deleted scene path canonical, demonstrating that a hash-current RAG can faithfully serve stale canon relative to implementation.
The Windows build has no registered scenes.
Current gameplay movement still directly polls WASD and does not use the planned mouse-directed Input Actions path.
Assignment 6 records two static-evaluator passes that remained unusable in Unity, followed by runtime-driven repairs and a no-op refinement rejection.
The clean Unity runner was created after a passing builder test destructively rewrote a tracked canonical scene.

On the current HEAD ancestry after Assignment 6, 244 commits added about 115,877 lines under Pipeline/Docs/Tasks, while only three commits touched Assets/Packages/ProjectSettings—and those addressed test safety and scene relocation, not a new gameplay feature.

Eleven selected deterministic GDDRAG, TaskGraph, TaskExecution, AgentRuntime/provider, process-runner, and testing-policy smoke/regression suites passed against the frozen clean tree. No Unity test was executed in this review environment.
Production GDDRAG is hash-current and integrity-valid with 41 chunks, correctly solving stale-index detection but not incorrect human canon.

gdd_iteration_concerns: A GDD edit updates neither existing task contracts nor resource references automatically. Rebuilding RAG only makes retrieval agree with the edited document.
Every delivered task currently binds the whole GDD hash, so an unrelated wording or design edit forces global revalidation rather than scoped impact analysis.
There is no operational state for an active attempt when canon changes: continue under its frozen contract, pause, supersede, or replan are human-only decisions with no implemented transaction.
The existing scene-path contradiction proves one-time bootstrap correctness does not provide ongoing synchronization.

Introduce stable requirement IDs and per-task requirement hashes. On a GDD change, classify linked planned work as needing replan and linked delivered work as needing targeted revalidation; leave unrelated work current.

Freeze the task-contract/canon revision for each active attempt. At a checkpoint, a human or explicit policy decides whether a relevant GDD change supersedes that attempt. Never silently retarget work in progress.
human_intervention_points: Choose product priority and approve task-contract clarifications. NSC-003 especially needs decisions on input arbitration, click/hold behavior, arrival/cancellation, and pathing.
Approve GDD changes and decide whether active work continues, is superseded, or needs remediation.
Operate or authorize the licensed Unity host and resolve project locks/import state.
Perform Play Mode feel, visual readability, camera framing, scene/prefab, sorting, and interaction checks.
Review and merge changes; retain this authority until several consecutive deliveries are reliable.
Currently, manually invoke a writable coding agent because the production adapters are read-only.
Currently, manually assemble/promote Unity results and conformance records after integration.
Acquire, approve, import, and visually integrate art/audio assets.
Worth automating next only after repeated use: Unity command/result capture, evidence-manifest generation, branch/attempt recovery, and requirement-impact alerts.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Parallel resource claims, multiple worktrees, merge queues, and GitHub synchronization protect a concurrency regime that does not exist yet.
Artifact Authority and Artifact GER protect future AI-authored design, but the current graph has no artifact task and no observed production blocker requiring it.
Progressive Decomposition addresses future coarse work; current execution fails before decomposition becomes the bottleneck.
Provider fallback and cross-provider review provenance do not advance a Unity ticket and are not yet production bottlenecks.
Much of AgentRuntime's adversarial JSON/subclass/path hardening protects theoretical provider-boundary attacks before providers have write authority.
The elaborate 15-auditor reconciliation/refinement/arbitration system protected a one-time bootstrap and should not become the routine response to GDD iteration.
Broad continuous-autonomy budgeting, backlog replenishment, and parallel scheduling are premature until one serial ticket can be delivered and recovered.
missing_components: One authoritative operational lifecycle ledger with attempt identity and explicit planned/running/validating/review/blocked/done/superseded states.
Evidence-derived dependency readiness tied to integrated delivery—not mutable task metadata.
A scoped writable implementer path with deterministic changed-file enforcement.
A real Unity-host execution adapter covering compilation, focused EditMode/PlayMode tests, and Windows build output.
Automatic evidence-manifest creation from actual Git and Unity results.
Branch/checkpoint/merge recovery that handles crashes and merged-but-unrecorded work idempotently.
Validation that task/resource/evidence paths still exist and agree with the current canonical scene registry.
Measured per-ticket elapsed time, human minutes, retries, token/cost use, and escaped-defect data.

deliverables: Human-freeze a narrow revision of NSC-005, resolving its duplicated/readability gates and specifying the smallest visible denied-mana feedback without expanding spell design.
Implement PlayerMana reset and denied-spend signaling plus the existing PlayerManaUI feedback consumer.
Extend PlayerMana Play Mode tests for reset, regeneration-delay reset, and denied-spend signaling.
Run the focused clean Unity PlayMode suite on the real host and perform one human readability check.
Merge through an ordinary branch and create one minimal delivery/evidence manifest using the existing mechanisms.
Record elapsed time, agent time, human minutes, retries, Unity import/test time, and manual edits.
next_slice.proof_of_value: From a clean checkout, deliver a visibly improved, tested, merged gameplay capability within one working day, with no repository mutation from tests and no more than roughly 60–90 minutes of human orchestration. Repeatability—not another schema—is the first credible evidence that weeks can become days.
next_slice.title: Actual game production: deliver NSC-005 end to end
next_slice.why: NSC-005 extends an existing small component and existing Play Mode suite, avoids NSC-003's unresolved input design, and isolates the real delivery bottleneck. Use an ordinary writable coding-agent workflow and the existing clean test/evidence pieces; do not build a supervisor first.

observed_failure_solutions: Repository-resident canon, contracts, logs, and decisions address real context/session loss and stale chat memory.
Production GDDRAG freshness/integrity addresses the actually stale July Assignment 4 index.
Reconciliation addressed stale Assignment 5 planning and found substantial semantic gaps before the initial graph was persisted.
GER runtime feedback solved camera defects missed by static evaluation.
The no-op progress guard and circuit breaker solve the observed refiner that claimed implementation without changing Assets.
The Unity testing policy and clean runner solve the observed passing test that rewrote a canonical scene.
Committed-scene conformance tests distinguish builder capability from actual serialized state, an observed source of false confidence.
Immutable run history and bounded recovery address timeouts/failures experienced while producing the reconciliation bootstrap.
overengineering: Approximately 23,059 lines of executable Python/PowerShell across the production pipeline areas versus about 1,508 lines of C# under Assets/NoSafeCircle, excluding generated reconciliation outputs.
A 15-auditor reconciliation pass, streaming field repairs, conflict arbitration, and extensive recovery machinery for a 37-contract one-time bootstrap.
Provider-neutral runtime and two live adapters were proven through ArchitectureReview rather than a writable gameplay ticket.
Strict immutable invocation publication and deep hostile-value validation are disproportionate before any provider can write or execute approved commands.
Thirty-seven detailed contracts were produced before the project had a current lifecycle/readiness model, and their embedded repository evidence is already stale.
Multiple long context documents retain superseded milestone/status semantics, increasing maintenance and authority ambiguity.
Whole-GDD conformance invalidation creates expensive revalidation work instead of precise safety.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries: human-approved design canon; immutable task scope/revision; integrated Git tree; deterministic Unity/Git evidence; worker claims; and explicit human visual/design approval.
The AgentRuntime/TaskExecution separation is appropriate: generic invocation should not fabricate NSC task identity.
Tasks correctly should define work rather than completion, but removing status without introducing an operational lifecycle authority leaves the graph inert.

Reconciliation snapshots, bootstrap repository observations, task-embedded GDD excerpts, RAG chunks, and current-state documents duplicate facts and can disagree; the scene-path drift demonstrates this.
Git should remain implementation authority, but delivery needs a single evidence manifest and materialized lifecycle state rather than several indirect records.
Do not add GitHub as a second mutable authority. If added, make it a one-way projection of the local lifecycle ledger.
Human approval is currently correctly retained for interactive quality, but manually recording approval inside hand-authored evidence JSON is costly and error-prone.
strong_decisions: Use deterministic code for identity, hashes, graph structure, Git facts, test parsing, and safety checks.
Treat provider/agent output as claims rather than completion evidence.
Keep workers bounded and begin with one serial worker.
Make Unity/runtime evidence capable of overriding static semantic approval.
Fail tests when they mutate the repository, even if assertions pass.
Separate builder-generation tests from committed-scene conformance tests.
Keep reconciliation snapshots immutable and prevent them from directly rewriting living work.
Fail closed on stale RAG indexes while acknowledging retrieval is not complete canon.
Keep final design, visual, play-feel, and merge authority human-owned for now.
structural_flaws: There is no end-to-end state transition from selected contract to writable execution, Unity validation, merge, evidence publication, and dependent readiness.

The first break without more infrastructure is immediate: taskcontrol will not produce a ready task and both providers reject writes/commands. If a human bypasses that boundary, task/canon ambiguity and drift break correctness next.
Schema-v2 removed completion state but no lifecycle authority replaced it, so the dependency graph cannot schedule anything.
Moving-target synchronization is not implemented; a clean structural validation passes despite deleted canonical paths throughout the graph and GDD.
Conformance uses a global GDD hash instead of task-relevant requirement identities, making routine iteration globally expensive.
Graph validation checks syntax and relationships but not whether referenced Unity paths or repository evidence remain current.
The production runtime has been proven on architecture review, not implementation, repair, Unity, or recovery of a gameplay ticket.
The Unity lane is a human-invoked Windows PowerShell wrapper, not an integrated execution/recovery service; Windows build settings are still empty.
Several supposedly single-agent contracts assert design completeness that the repository's own current-state document later disputes, particularly NSC-003.
Canonical architecture/status documentation contradicts itself about readiness, milestone order, and scene authority.
No throughput telemetry establishes that the additional infrastructure reduces elapsed time or human effort.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: The current system cannot turn weeks into days because it cannot autonomously start or deliver a gameplay task. Its strongest production proof is one camera feature whose static checks passed twice while Unity remained unusable, requiring two human runtime failures and three refinements. Since that work, HEAD ancestry contains 244 commits and roughly 115,877 added lines under Pipeline/Docs/Tasks but no new gameplay feature. The architecture may eventually reduce rediscovery, unsafe testing, and recovery cost, but major leverage requires repeated end-to-end delivery. A credible threshold is two or three consecutive small gameplay tickets delivered in a day each with bounded retries and under about 60–90 minutes of human orchestration per ticket.
structured_output.verdict_reason: Keep the bounded-worker, deterministic-validation, RAG freshness, Unity safety, and evidence ideas. Reject the current investment sequence and moving-canon model. The project has optimized review, provenance, and hypothetical autonomy risks before implementing the one transaction that creates value: safely turning an approved gameplay change into a tested, playable, merged increment.
